Q1: It means you tried to grant a level the user already holds, or a greater one. No remediation is needed; the user already has that access.
Q2: Changing model access requires model admin access on that model, or controller superuser access.
Q3: Changing offer access requires model admin access on the model the offer belongs to, or controller superuser access.
Q4: Revoking the `read` level deletes the permission record outright, so it is the same write as removing the grant.
Q5: No. The revoke fails with `user is the last model admin for 1 or more models`; first grant admin on the model to another user.
Q6: Ten level-object pairs are valid. For offers the valid levels are `read`, `consume` and `admin`.
Q7: An external user's effective level is the greater of their own grants and those of `everyone@external`. This is resolved on each access check; nothing is stored or cached.
Q8: No. Granting or revoking cloud access for yourself fails with `cannot change your own cloud access`; ask another cloud admin or a controller superuser.
Q9: The natural key is the pair of object and user.
Q10: Granting to an external user that Juju has not seen yet creates that user as a side effect, so the permission record has someone to name.
Q11: No. The access domain exposes no change streams; user and permission changes are read on demand.
Q12: The provider's `jaas_access_controller` resource (with `jaas_access_cloud` for clouds) manages controller access, and they apply when using JAAS.
Q13: The client validates before sending and refuses a controller level paired with a model or offer, with the error `You have specified a controller access permission "<level>"...`. Name a model or offer level, or drop the model or offer.
